newsitem.title: USA: Westell, Amati confirm role in MCI plan.
newsitem.headline: Westell, Amati confirm role in MCI plan.

text.p: Several suppliers of advanced telecommunications equipment confirmed Thursday they were taking part with MCI Communications Corp and Northwest Iowa Telephone in an alliance to bring local phone, Internet and other services to rural America.

Westell, a supplier of Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) systems said the alliance had begun testing its FlexCap ADSL products in a system that would allow MCI employees high-speed access from their homes to MCI's corporate network.
Amati Communications Corp and NEC Corp's NEC America Inc said they too were participating in the plan.

Amati and NEC America said they have been working on a trial of Amati's ADSL equipment with MCI and Northwest Iowa Telephone since July 1996 to offer broadcast quality television delivered over local telephone phone lines.
The test uses the Amati six megabit-per-second ADSL/DMT modems together with the video switching equipment provided by NEC America.
The trial marks the first deployment in the United States of real-time six megabit full-motion, switched digital video, they said.

Test results to date have shown that ADSL is a technically viable method for transmitting broadcast TV services over the copper wire loop that connects homes and telephone central office switching equipment, the companies said.
The initial Westell ADSL trial involves MCI customer service representatives located in Sergeant Bluff, Iowa.
ADSL modems enable these off-site employees to work with customer files on the central office computer at speeds up to 50 times faster than a standard 28.8 kilobit modem.
